title: Beyond topology-based graph mining: Deep analysis research networks via evolutionary topology and content fusion
abstract: Research data mining, a task which encompasses multiple document types (e.g., academic papers or patents), has garnered significant attention in the current research landscape. It aims to extract valuable information from the ever-growing body of research literature to uncover knowledge associations. However, existing studies have limitations in analyzing citation motivations and primarily focus on pairwise relationships between documents, which constrains accurate prediction of knowledge dissemination and interpretable analysis. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a graph-text model based on citation networks (GTCN), which uses large language models (LLMs) to learn from textual information and explore the underlying motivations behind citation. We introduce a progressive learning strategy to capture global network structures, generating node embeddings that reflect multi-aspect influences. On this basis, we further propose an attention fusion embedding (AFE) module, which aggregates node representations along semantically meaningful citation paths to model specific aspects of influence. This approach effectively overcomes the limitations of traditional methods that focus solely on binary relationship prediction, enabling in-depth exploration of technological pathways across different research contexts. We conduct experiments on five datasets, including both academic paper and patent citation networks, extending the typical pairwise link prediction task to a path-aware N-path prediction task. On node classification, GTCN achieves state-of-the-art results, outperforming other hybrid LLM-GNN methods by a margin of up to 6.03 % and 4.20 % in the F1 score on the Cora and PubMed datasets, respectively. Through visual analytics, we validate GTCN’s interpretability analysis capability, highlighting the immense potential of GTCN in analyzing citation networks for research data mining.
rationale: 通过LLM编码论文和专利文本，并结合演化引文网络预测知识传播路径、解释引文动机；科学知识演化研究是明确研究任务，AI实质参与。
